newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK ACCUSES SIX IN "MAJOR HORSERACE-FIXING SCANDAL".
newsitem.headline: HK ACCUSES SIX IN "MAJOR HORSERACE-FIXING SCANDAL".

text.p: Six Hong Kong people, including a businessman, appeared in court on Friday in connection with the territory's biggest alleged horse race-fixing scandal for 10 years.
With an annual betting turnover equivalent to $US 11 billion, horse-racing in Hong Kong is one of the world's busiest and the colony's only legal form of gambling.
Altogether 39 people, including jockeys and trainers, were arrested after a probe by graft-busting police of the Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) in March.
They were detained by an anti-corruption squad swooping during a race meeting at Sha Tin track, one of Hong Kong's two courses, and in raids on a number of premises.
Police say they are still investigating an alleged syndicated race-fixing system.

Among the six charged was 33-year-old businessman Ng Siu-chau, who faces two counts of betting with a bookmaker, which is illegal. Punters can only bet at the track with monopoly Hong Jockey Club outlets.

Ng, who made no plea, will appear in court again soon with three other defendants who earlier denied similar charges. Their case will be transferred to a higher-level Court, said an ICAC spokesman who refused to enlarge on the scale of the alleged race-fixing.
Another two suspects, who also pleaded not guilty on Friday, will appear at a separate future hearing.
